item.title: 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk, Cowboys' Jake Ferguson reportedly win appeals of drink-chugging TD celebration fines
item.description: Juszczyk was successful in appealing the $14,926 fine by the league.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson will reportedly be getting back the money that they were fined by the NFL after what it believed were beer-chugging celebrations.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the players won their appeals after Juszczyk said that he was pretending to drink a juice box, not a beer and Ferguson said his was a Gatorade celebration that he had used in the past.

"Mr. Juszczyk finally stated that the fine is hypocritical with the amount of Bud Light sponsorships surrounding the NFL," read part of the letter referencing the league's reported $250 million per deal with Anheuser-Busch InBev.

Juszczyk, whose nickname is "Juice," caught a six-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter of the 49ers' 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2. After celebrating with teammates, Juszczyk turned back toward the crowd while in the end zone and imitated chugging a drink.

— NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026

He did the celebration later in the game and received two fines for $14,926 apiece that week.

"I don't know how else to say it: I wasn't drinking beer in my celebration," Juszczyk told reporters after the news was reported. "I think you guys all know my nickname is 'Juice.' I have juice on my pads. The stadium yells 'Juice' when I catch the ball. When I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice, and it's been that way for years. So I was surprised as anybody when I got a fine this week."

Juszczyk won't be on the field for a few weeks to add to his juice box celebration total for the season. After hyperextending his knee on Sunday, he is set to miss time.

Ferguson was docked $13,611 after the league interpreted his Week 2 touchdown celebration against the Washington Commanders as him shotgunning a beer.

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jets fans and fans across the country.

This season has taken a difficult turn for the New York Jets and their fans. A year that began with a promising win over the Tennessee Titans has gone off track with three consecutive losses. If the Jets lose in Week 5 to the Cleveland Browns, fans will once again be looking to the Draft in mid-October.

This has led to questions about head coach Aaron Glenn’s job status. Glenn’s first year did not go well as the Jets stumbled to a 3-14 record. Time will tell what this team’s famously erratic ownership will do, but this week in our SB Nation Reacts polls, we want your opinion on what the Jets should do with Glenn.

item.title: ESPN insider offers 2 Detroit Lions trade target suggestion
item.description: ESPN listed two defensive backs the Detroit Lions should consider trading for.
item.content:encoded:
After being significant players in the trade talks for Joey Porter Jr.—but ultimately missing out—the Detroit Lions must go back to the drawing board if they want to upgrade their struggling secondary.

Last week, we offered our own suggestions that Lions general manager Brad Holmes should consider. On Wednesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler offered two more trade targets Detroit should consider.

“One potential option is Kansas City’s Kristian Fulton, who is in and out of the Chiefs’ lineup,” Fowler wrote. “He is owed real money — $5 million of his $9.75 million base salary is guaranteed — but perhaps the Chiefs and Lions could split the bill to facilitate a deal. Is it worth calling Pittsburgh for Jalen Ramsey? Not sure he’s available, but the Lions’ defense seems far from settled.”

Let’s handle these one by one.

Fulton was the Titans’ second-round pick in 2020. After starting 37 games over four years in Tennessee, he signed a one-year deal with the Chargers in 2024. There, he produced a strong season: 51 tackles, seven passes defended, an interception, and a 68.9 PFF grade, ranking him 32nd out of 80 qualifying cornerbacks.

Fulton parlayed that success into a two-year, $20 million deal with the Chiefs last year, but it turned out to be a failed year for him. A knee injury caused him to miss most of the offseason program, he dealt with a Week 2 ankle injury, and then essentially lost his job. He was a healthy scratch for about a third of the season, playing in just eight games and starting two.

This year, Fulton has played more, but is not a full-time player. He’s logged 115 defensive snaps through four games, including a Week 3 contest against the Dolphins in which he did not play a single snap for reasons that are unclear. Despite the part-time gig, Fulton has held up well. He’s produced a 76.0 overall PFF grade and a 76.4 coverage grade. He’s been targeted eight times and allowed just four catches for 19 yards and an interception—though he does already have two penalties.

Fulton’s usage is certainly peculiar, but it could suggest the Chiefs would be willing to move on. Fulton is a physical, handsy cornerback with average size (5-foot-11, 197 pounds) and acceptable speed (4.46 40-yard dash).

As for Ramsey, his history of success is well documented. Since entering the league in 2016, he’s an eight-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro. He’ll turn 32 later this month and certainly isn’t in the prime of his career, but he’s still producing at a strong level. From 2024-25, he produced 148 tackles, 19 pass breakups and three interceptions.

But if you’re hoping that helps the Lions’ outside cornerback situation, he may not be the guy you’re looking for. Ramsey has mostly played as a nickel corner or safety with the Steelers this year—a transition he’s been making over the last two seasons. Could the Lions still use help at those positions? Absolutely. But if you want an upgrade on the perimeter, Ramsey is probably not the answer.

As for financials, Ramsey wouldn’t come cheap. He’s currently sporting a $17.5 million salary—and that number jump to $19.7 in 2027 and $22 million in 2028—so it would likely be just a one-year rental for Detroit.

item.title: Chiefs P Matt Araiza named the AFC special teams player of the week
item.description: Chiefs punter Matt Araiza used his feet to help the team in multiple ways in Week 4.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs punter Matt Araiza used his feet to help the team in multiple ways in Week 4.

Araiza had five punts against the Raiders and all of them landed inside of the Las Vegas 20-yard-line with one pinning the Raiders inside the 5-yard-line. Araiza also converted a fake punt with a 12-yard run in the first quarter of the 30-27 win.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that Araiza has been named the AFC special teams player of the week. It's the first time that Araiza has earned that honor.

Araiza averaged 47.6 yards per punt last Sunday and is averaging 52.3 yards per kick for the entire season.

item.title: NFL news, live updates: Lamar Jackson uncertain to play Week 5 due to ankle injury; Eagles All-Pro RT Lane Johnson announces retirement; Seahawks won't sign Joe Mixon
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news coming out of Week 4.
item.content:encoded:
Week 4 is officially in the books following Monday night's NFC South showdown, where the Atlanta Falcons demolished the New Orleans Saints on the road with a 45-24 win. Bijan and Brian Robinson combined for five rushing touchdowns on the night to tie the franchise record for most in a single game, last accomplished back in 2008. Sorry, fantasy football managers. Brian got three, while Bijan got two.

Several stars went down with injuries this week, which should have NFL fans on notice for Week 5, headlined by Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, who left the stadium in a walking boot after suffering an ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Jackson suffered an ankle sprain and has an "outside" chance of playing in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons.

Also worth monitoring: running back Saquon Barkley exited Week 4 with a hamstring injury and is reportedly considered "week-to-week," while the Cincinnati Bengals saw both Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) suffer injuries this week.

The Kansas City Chiefs also lost two of their top receivers Sunday, too, as Rashee Rice went down with a hamstring issue and Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury that will keep him out 12-16 weeks. Per The Athletic's Michael Silver, the team has reached out to Tyreek Hill's agent about a possible reunion.

While it may not be injury news, the Philadelphia Eagles got some relatively surprising news as All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement on Tuesday. He played in the first three games of the season before being a surprise inactive for Week 4 due to personal reasons. The veteran was in his 14th season.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 4.

item.title: Deonte Banks named NFC defensive player of the week
item.description: Giants cornerback Deonte Banks put an exclamation point on the Giants’ victory over the Cardinals with a 98-yard pick-six as time expired.
item.content:encoded:
Giants cornerback Deonte Banks put an exclamation point on the Giants’ victory over the Cardinals with a 98-yard pick-six as time expired.

He’s now been named NFC defensive player of the week.

Banks had four total tackles with four passes defended and his interception returned for a touchdown.

Banks is the first Giants cornerback to be named defensive player of the week since 2019.

The Giants will be on the road to face the Commanders in Week 5.

item.title: Jaguars LB Foye Oluokun is the AFC defensive player of the week
item.description: The Jaguars continued their impressive start to the season against the Bengals last Sunday and linebacker Foye Oluokun was integral to their success.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars continued their impressive start to the season against the Bengals last Sunday and linebacker Foye Oluokun was integral to their success.

Oluokun had seven tackles, an interception, a forced fumble and a quarterback hit to help the Jags to a 22-17 win. The interception came at Jacksonville's 10-yard-line early in the fourth quarter and kept the Jaguars up 16-10 heading into the final minutes of the contest.

On Wednesday, the NFL announced that Oluokun has been named the AFC defensive player of the week.

It is the fourth time Oluokun has been awarded conference player of the week honors. The first two came while he was with the Falcons and the last two have come since he moved on to the Jaguars.

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan wins first NFC offensive player of the week award
item.description: Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan was dominant in Sunday's victory over the Lions and now the league has recognized him for his performance.
item.content:encoded:
Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan was dominant in Sunday's victory over the Lions and now the league has recognized him for his performance.

McMillan has been named NFC offensive player of the week.

McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards with two touchdowns in the 32-26 victory, setting career highs in both catches and yards.

McMillan is the first receiver in Panthers franchise history to win NFC offensive player of the week.

He tied the Panthers franchise record for receptions in a single game on Sunday.

McMillan will get a chance to rest after so many catches, as he and the Panthers have a Week 5 bye.

item.title: Commanders roster news: Two signed to practice squad; QB gets workout
item.description: Commanders make several moves as injuries continue to mount
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders had two players from their practice squad poached this week. Unrafted free agent RB Robert Henry Jr. signed with the Seahawks, and veteran CB Terell Smith was signed by the Steelers. The Commanders roster was expected to have a few changes with WR/KR Jaylin Lane going to injured reserve after suffering a serious ankle dislocation and Marcus Mariota reinjuring his MCL.

The Commanders worked out QB Jack Plummer this morning per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. He noted that the tream isn’t placing Mariota on IR, and said they weren’t planning on signing Plummer. He’s an option if needed later in the season. Mariota originally sprained his MCL in the first preseason game against the Dolphins. He didn’t play again until Jayden Daniels was injured in Week 2. The team has their bye in Week 7 giving them additional time for Mariota to return without needing to use an IR designation.

Washington also announced two roster moves to fill the two open spots on their practice squad. OLB T.J. Maguranyanga has been with the team as their International Pathways Program player, but Washington used that roster exemption for DT Jeffrey M’ba this year. Now he returns as a regular member of the practice squad, signing today along with S Darren Hall.

The Commanders are also signing WR Nick DeGennaro to the practice squad per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. This move isn’t official, and the team will need to make another roster move to open up a spot.

item.title: Odell Beckham Jr. signs with Vikings' practice squad after release by Giants
item.description: Beckham did not record a catch in three games during his return to the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Odell Beckham Jr. has signed with the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, the team announced Wednesday.

The 33-year-old was released by the New York Giants on Sept. 29. He played in three games after returning to the team that drafted him in 2014 and didn't record a reception. In those three games, Beckham was on the field for a total of 20 offensive snaps, with just six of those coming in his final game with the team, a 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 3.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell was Beckham's offensive coordinator when the two were with the Los Angeles Rams in 2021 when the team won Super Bowl LVI.

In eight regular-season games with the Rams, Beckham had 27 receptions for 305 yards and five touchdowns. He added 21 catches for 288 yards and two touchdowns in the postseason before he tore his ACL in the Super Bowl against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The 4-0 Vikings take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 and there is still uncertainty about the status of Justin Jefferson. The All-Pro wide receiver missed Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins with an ankle sprain. O'Connell said Tuesday that Jefferson was "doing great," but they are not sure yet how the wideout will feel on Sunday.

item.title: Drake Maye named the AFC offensive player of the week
item.description: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's first three games raised a lot of red flags around New England, but they are harder to find after last Sunday's win over the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's first three games raised a lot of red flags around New England, but they are harder to find after last Sunday's win over the Bills.

Maye went 22-of-37 for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including one that wide receiver Efton Chism used one hand to secure for the winning points in a 29-26 victory. Maye also ran eight times for 54 yards.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that the performance landed Maye recognition as the AFC offensive player of the week. It is the second time that Maye has won the award.

Maye did have a pair of turnovers in the game after having seven in the first three games, so there's still some work to do to get back to his 2025 level of play. The overall effort provided reason to believe that can happen and that was the best development of the week for the Patriots.

item.title: With Braiden McGregor injured, Jets sign Nate Lynn to active roster
item.description: Edge defender Braiden McGregor is out for the season after tearing a pectoral muscle in the team’s Week 4 loss to the Chicago Bears. Replacing him on the roster is a familiar name to Jets fans, Nate Lynn. Lynn signed with the team during the summer a few weeks into training camp. He seemed like […]
item.content:encoded:
Edge defender Braiden McGregor is out for the season after tearing a pectoral muscle in the team’s Week 4 loss to the Chicago Bears. Replacing him on the roster is a familiar name to Jets fans, Nate Lynn.

Lynn signed with the team during the summer a few weeks into training camp. He seemed like the longest of long shots to make the team at the time, but played his way into legitimate contention with a strong preseason. Lynn posted 3 sacks in the final two exhibition games. While McGregor ultimately got the nod for the final edge defender spot on the roster, Lynn was signed to the practice squad.

It will be interesting to see whether Lynn is used differently from McGregor. While McGregor did start earning some time on passing situations, the Jets also utilized him on early downs to do the dirty work setting the edge. To this point, Lynn has seemed more like a pass rusher.

Either way, I do expect Lynn to get snaps in Week 5 against the Cleveland Browns.

item.title: Giants sign QB Jake Haener to their 53-man roster, per report
item.description: Jake Haener joins the Giants’ active roster, giving the team three quarterbacks.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants are signing backup quarterback Jake Haener to their 53-man roster, per a report from Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network. This fills the roster spot opened by the loss of wide receiver/kick returner Braxton Berrios.

The Giants singed Haener on Aug. 17 following some disastrous preseason performances by Brandon Allen. Haener, 27, is a former fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints in the 2023 NFL Draft. He spent time as the Saints’ starting quarterback in 2024 after Derek Carr’s Week 14 injury, but was waived and signed to the Saints’ practice squad in 2025.

Haener played well enough for the Giants in the final preseason game and was ultimately signed to the practice squad instead of Allen.

Haener now likely becomes the Giants’ primary backup while J.J. McCarthy gets up to speed. This does raise the question as to whether or not the Giants will employ their “McCarthy package” against the Washington Commanders.

This also opens up a spot on the Giants’ practice squad. The Giants did have a visit on Tuesday from wide receiver Dontae Fleming, who spent last season on the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad.

item.title: Early Week 5 NFL betting, odds: 2 wagers that I like right now
item.description: Our NFL handicapper gives two Week 5 bets he likes at the moment.
item.content:encoded:
Looking at early bets for Week 5, there is less in the market than I would normally attack for two key reasons. The first is that injuries continue to pile up around the league, and so many of these teams and markets are defined by which way the mid-week practice reports and news go, dictating who is healthy enough to play. Those news breaks will drastically impact the line movements. I don't have more information than what is publicly available, and would simply be applying my best guess to the market. That is sometimes a really good idea but nothing presents itself strongly for doing so now (maybe Atlanta Falcons +2.5 thinking Lamar Jackson can't go).

The second is that bye weeks have begun — the Chiefs and Panthers will be off this week — and thus we have one less game to attack as well.

Here are two Week 5 bets that I have found actionable.

Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams (-2.5, 54.5)

Starting off with the injury updates, the Rams came out of their Week 4 comeback win over the Philadelphia Eagles pretty much unscathed.

Star wideout Puka Nacua looked fantastic and reported no setbacks (he had 12 targets, nine receptions, 125 yards and a 2-yard rushing touchdown). Aaron Donald might be back for the Rams after missing last game with back soreness. On the other side, the Bills dealt with more injuries to WR DJ Moore, DT Ed Oliver, CB Christian Benford and safety Jordan Poyer. Losing Moore might be OK considering the rise of Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid this season, but the defensive injuries are a real problem. Matthew Stafford will be able to lean on a strong run game to create clean pockets. I think the Rams move the ball effortlessly here.

Bet the Los Angeles Rams to cover the spread at sportsbooks

I am very surprised this line is not at -3 yet and think it will close there, making the -2.5 a very valuable grab early in the week. The Rams took market action late in the week against the Eagles, closing at -3.5 on the road, and the Patriots took action down from +7.5 to +6.5 at kickoff against the Bills last week (while New England was also dealing with some key injuries).

Both the Rams won and covered, and the Bills lost outright, and I expect those market patterns to continue.

Bet: L.A. Rams -2.5 (-118)

Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 44)

After four weeks, one of my biggest adjustments against preseason priors is higher on the Steelers offense, and lower on their defense.

Aaron Rodgers is throwing the ball further downfield this year with revamped offensive weapons and it clearly shows in his average depth of target (aDOT) stats. His aDOT has risen from 6.0 yards per attempt last season to 10.0 this season. This is something that new head coach Mike McCarthy has specifically referenced about changing within the offense, and the addition of Michael Pittman Jr. and rise of Roman Wilson are key reasons to make that possible. On the defensive side of the ball, the obvious first point is trading away their top man coverage defensive back Joey Porter Jr.

However, the run defense has dropped off significantly as well. The Steelers D allows 113 rushing yards per game — just about average for the NFL, and a near top-10 in efficiency in 4.3 yards per carry. This defense has been historically elite at stopping the run, and has regressed to the middle of the pack. Now, they face an Indianapolis Colts team with elite RB Jonathan Taylor (off a two-touchdown game in London) and the sixth-best red zone efficiency metrics in the NFL.

The Colts have a strong offensive scheme under head coach Shane Steichen; they move the ball well between the 20s and convert when they are close. The Indianapolis offense has scored above its implied team total in three of its four games this season, and I expect that to continue.

Bet: Colts-Steelers over 44

item.title: Alec Pierce’s prolonged absence is killing the Colts
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts are facing a bit of a crisis at the wide receiver position. Michael Pittman Jr. was traded this offseason. He didn’t seem to have his best stuff anymore, but that one still hurt. Alec Pierce was tabbed to be the next man to take over the reins as the number one receiver. […]
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts are facing a bit of a crisis at the wide receiver position. Michael Pittman Jr. was traded this offseason. He didn’t seem to have his best stuff anymore, but that one still hurt. Alec Pierce was tabbed to be the next man to take over the reins as the number one receiver. Since cashing his check, we have hardly seen him on the field. The Colts are feeling the effects.

Statistically, Daniel Jones had his worst quarter and a half against the Commanders. There was pressure, but his attempts were the shortest in the league at 3.8 per play. Going 19/34 for only 143 yards and multiple turnovers proves Jones is struggling. Josh Downs is the twitchy man the Colts need underneath, but no one can take the top off the defense. Laquon Treadwell has been the Colts’ best downfield threat. No offense to Treadwell, but he isn’t going to cut it.

Pierce was the deep threat. Last year, he added more routes and became more of a well-rounded receiver. That made his deep threat even more lethal. Jones averaged over 8 yards per attempt last year with Pierce in the fold. Not only would Pierce provide an option for a deep shot, he also opened the rest of the field by taking defenders with him away from the line of scrimmage. His presence on the outside changes everything. Another heel injury is crippling the Colts.

Alec Pierce may or may not be a true number one, but his importance to the Colts is real. Occupying a corner and safety deep while providing an option to pick up huge yards in a hurry is something the Colts can’t replicate without him. He was supposed to be the guy. Missing time this year doesn’t mean he can’t be going forward, but being without him means the offense, Daniel Jones very much included, is going to feel the effects.

item.title: Ravens Week 4 film study: Vega Ioane could be a long-term center
item.description: The Ravens’ Week 4 game tape showed a budding young pass rush and Vega Ioane’s potential at center.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens’ gritty Week 4 win over the Titans gave us another opportunity to evaluate several players in the trenches on both sides of the football. Mike Green stepped into a larger role as Baltimore’s primary edge rusher on passing downs, Nnamdi Madubuike continued to show that he has returned to form, and rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane provided some much-needed stability along the interior offensive line in his first start at center.

OLB Mike Green

40 snaps | 26 pass rush | 13 run defense | 1 coverage | 5 pressures

With Trey Hendrickson out, Mike Green was expected to take on a larger role as a pass rusher, and he delivered. Green finished with five pressures while posting a 29.4% win rate on true pass sets, but one of the more interesting developments was the power he flashed throughout the game.

On one rep, Green held a firm edge before using a rip move to work around the offensive tackle and make the tackle. On another, he struck the tackle with heavy hands, stood him up at the point of attack and worked off the block to make the play. Those reps were encouraging because Green’s game has largely been built around his quickness, hand usage and ability to win around the edge.

As a pass rusher, Green continued to flash the cross chop that has become one of his most dependable moves. The timing of that move has gotten close to automatic, but he also showed some development within his pass-rush plan. On one rep, Green used a hesitation into a cross chop to open the offensive tackle’s hips before countering with an inside spin and generating pressure on the quarterback. On another, he converted speed to power, got inside the tackle’s chest and drove him backward into the quarterback’s lap.

The encouraging part of Green’s performance was the variety. We already knew he could win with quickness and his cross chop, but adding legitimate power and counters gives tackles more to think about when trying to protect against him. As the season progresses, Green becoming a dependable pass-rush option will be important if the Ravens want to consistently generate pressure without Trey Hendrickson on the field.

DT Nnamdi Madubuike

46 snaps | 16 run defense | 30 pass rush | 6 pressures

Nnamdi Madubuike has started to pick things up over the last few weeks, and considering where he was physically a year ago, his return to form has been impressive. For a player who was facing the possibility of medical retirement, Madubuike looks as strong and explosive as he has at any point in his career.

He finished the game with six pressures and recorded a 20% win rate on true pass sets. His ability to convert speed to power remains one of the most dangerous parts of his game. Madubuike has the athleticism to threaten offensive linemen off the snap before turning that momentum into power and collapsing the interior of the pocket.

That strength also showed up against the run. One of the more important aspects of Madubuike’s game has always been his ability to handle combination blocks, engage double teams and find ways to split offensive linemen. On one rep, he established inside leverage against the blocker before working his way into the backfield and helping force the running back into a minimal gain.

Madubuike’s return has been great to see, but more importantly, his presence changes what Baltimore can do up front. Interior pressure forces quarterbacks off their spot and prevents them from simply stepping up when Baltimore’s edge rushers win around the corner. If Madubuike continues playing at this level, he will be a major piece of the Ravens developing a more consistent pass rush as the season progresses.

C Vega Ioane

64 snaps | 30 run blocking | 34 pass blocking | 0 pressures allowed

Vega Ioane made his first start at center this season, and there was a lot to like about what he showed. Ioane played all 64 offensive snaps and did not allow a pressure despite matching up with Jeffery Simmons multiple times throughout the game.

One of Ioane’s biggest strengths is his ability to operate in close quarters. He does a good job preventing defensive linemen from getting clean access to his chest, while his punch timing and hand fighting allow him to maintain leverage and keep defenders at length. That showed up repeatedly against Simmons, where Ioane was able to absorb contact without surrendering significant ground in pass protection.

His ability to quickly flip his hips also translates well to center. Ioane has the core strength to absorb power while maintaining his balance, and his movement skills allow him to redirect defenders once he establishes contact.

One rep in particular highlighted the combination of technique and athleticism that makes Ioane intriguing inside. Ioane used a snatch technique to throw the defensive lineman to the ground before immediately working downfield on a screen. It was a good example of his ability to win the initial engagement and then transition into his next assignment.

The biggest takeaway from Ioane’s first start at center was stability. Baltimore’s interior offensive line has desperately needed reliable play, and allowing zero pressures over 34 pass-blocking snaps against a defensive front featuring Jeffery Simmons is an encouraging start. If Ioane can continue providing that level of pass protection while developing the finer details of playing center, the Ravens may have found an answer at a position that entered the season with plenty of uncertainty.

item.title: Week 5 Stripes of the Week: McNeese
item.description: Five debutants earn Stripes of the Week.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re new to the series, David Billiot Jr. and I snake-draft to hand out Stripes of the Week for our podcast, Geaux Deep Dive. The first picks get three stripes, the second picks get two, and the last picks get one, highlighting our top performers of the week.

Five of the six players this week made their Stripes debut. So, here are Week 5’s Stripes of the Week:

Three Stripes: Harlem Berry (Zach) and Deuce Geralds (David)

It has been an interesting start to the season for Harlem Berry. Starting the season as RB3, the former five-star recruit carried the ball only five times for 13 yards against Clemson and Louisiana Tech and did not record a stat against Ole Miss. One of the big things that Lane Kiffin has harped on is blocking, and Berry has shown more willingness to block, and he has been rewarded with more touches. When Texas A&M came around, Berry got the opportunity to play RB2 behind Dilin Jones, and he has averaged 8.3 yards per carry since. Against McNeese, Berry had 15 carries for 125 yards, including one touchdown, flashing that big-play ability Tiger fans knew he had. Berry understandably wants to be RB1, but the fact that Kiffin and Charlie Weis Jr. are forcing him to develop his game will make Berry a much better player in the long run.

Typically, in victories with a large margin, we like to highlight some players who may not be in the conversation every single week. That was the idea when Deuce Geralds was awarded three stripes in Week 1 against Clemson. Since then, Geralds has cemented himself in the conversation every single week. The true freshman has had an incredible start to the season. One sack on the evening puts Geralds’ total for the season at five, just 2.5 sacks shy of tying Harold Perkins’ freshman single-season record of 7.5. Let’s also not forget the rushing touchdown Geralds added to his resume from a direct snap on the goal line. The production and the personality have made the Georgia native a fan favorite quickly, drawing some high praise and elite player comparisons.

Two Stripes: Corey Barber Jr. (David) and Stacy Gage (Zach)

The leading receiver from Saturday was another true freshman, Corey Barber Jr., who tallied seven catches for 83 yards and two scores. His performance did not come late in the game either, as both of his touchdown receptions came from Sam Leavitt. With so much talent of a similar level in the wide receiver room, it can be difficult to break through and emerge as an option on this team, but Barber could very well be in line for some more playing time with the starters following his performance.

Judging purely by the box score, Stacy Gage could have been a candidate for three stripes, but most of his stats came when the game was already out of hand. That is not at all to diminish his six carries for 110 yards and two touchdowns. Gage had a very good performance, making some unbelievable cuts on his big runs. His blocking ability and his talent in the run game are why it has been so difficult for players like Harlem Berry and Caden Durham to get their touches. This run game has improved greatly from last season for many reasons, but one is certainly the three-headed monster LSU is building in the backfield.

One Stripe: Roman Mothershed (Zach) and Tylen Singleton (David)

Since LSU signed Roman Mothershed out of the transfer portal, he is someone I have had my eye on. A wide receiver who is 6-foot-5 and 208 pounds is not something you see every day, and his limited tape was very fun to watch, but there was certainly some development that needed to be done. Then Trey’Dez Green went down with an injury, and eyes quickly turned to Mothershed, whose size is comparable to that of Green, to fill the void. It took about a week, but Mothershed, with his two catches for 11 yards and a score from the one-yard line, showed why everyone quickly looked to him when Green went down. It was a play that LSU had run numerous times for Green in that situation. The one stripe may be a bit of forecasting or wishcasting, but seeing LSU run that play with Mothershed gives confidence that someone can fill portions of the void left by Green until he returns from injury.

With the linebacker room dealt a brutal hand of injuries, including Whit Weeks and Charles Ross, someone had to step up. Both Tylen Singleton and Zach Weeks played fairly well against McNeese.Singleton, Weeks and Dylan Carpenter tied for the team lead with five tackles, but Singleton gets the edge with four solo tackles and one tackle for loss. Singleton highlighted a smothering defensive performance that, had it not been for Jamaal Levi, would have been a near-perfect game for Blake Baker’s defense.

Honorable Mentions:

Zach Weeks: Five tackles

Dylan Carpenter: Five tackles

Dominic McKinley: One sack, two tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss

Tamarcus Cooley: One interception, one tackle

Jayce Brown: Four receptions, 52 yards

item.title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Houston comeback, Nick Sorensen, defensive sacks
item.description: Here is our latest roundtable with a panel of BTB writers giving us their answers to this week’s questions
item.content:encoded:
Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. 

What was most convincing about the comeback win? 

Mike – The most convincing part was Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas looked flat, stuck, and out of answers in the first half, but Schottenheimer helped flip the game after halftime. The play-calling became much better, the offense found rhythm, and the team clearly still believed it could win even when Houston had control.

Credit has to go to the head coach when adjustments work and the team responds. This was not just Dak Prescott or CeeDee Lamb dragging Dallas out of trouble. It was a coaching staff finding answers, and Schotty did that. 

Dyllan – If teams choose to eliminate the quick death by focusing on George Pickens, Dallas is happy to methodically beat you with CeeDee Lamb the entire game. And don’t forget about Flournoy, by the way, who is completely capable of key chain moving grabs. This WR room reminded the NFL why they’re so dangerous.

Jorge – The offense genuinely looks like a force of nature, and I still don’t think it’s firing on all cylinders yet. To Dyllan’s point, the WR room may be the deepest and most capable in the league, and they are getting the job done when called up and asked to deliver in the clutch. Oh, and QB Dak Prescott ain’t playing too bad either. 

Tom – I’m not sure there was anything convincing besides the obvious potency of the passing attack, and a nice bit of evidence that CeeDee is indeed among the elite at his position. But a couple of other things were at least encouraging. The red zone offense found a way every time. And the Cowboys had half the penalties, not their normal result. Oddly, those two are kind of interconnected, because on one touchdown the Texans just refused to get off the field without getting a flag.

Sean – The offense not being denied in crunch time. The margin for error on some of Dak’s biggest throws of the game was slim to none, and every point the Cowboys put up ended up being needed. We can keep hoping and dreaming to see this offense with a little less pressure on their backs to score almost every time they touch it, but for now they’re scoring at an elite rate anyway, and it’s good enough to be right in the thick of things going into mid-October.

Are we happy with how Nick Sorensen is coaching the special teams unit?

Mike – In my opinion he needs to go. Brandon Aubrey is elite, but Aubrey’s leg should not cover up the wider special teams problems. The unit has too many messy moments, too many avoidable mistakes, and too many situations where Dallas either loses hidden yards or puts unnecessary pressure on the rest of the team. Special teams should be the cleanest, most reliable phase, not something that constantly feels like it is one mistake away from hurting the Cowboys. At some point, the coordinator has to own that. 

Dyllan – The FG unit needs to learn how to block things up in a hurry. They nearly had a second kick blocked on the PAT at the end of the game. But I do love their mastery of the dirty kick. The hidden yards in field position is extremely important for the growing defense. And Turpin is quietly putting up solid return numbers. I’m fine with Sorensen but they do need to figure out how to block on the FG attempts.

Jorge – No. Special teams was an issue last year, and continues to be this year. The kickoff penalties are unacceptable, and blocked field goals played a hand in a loss this year. Aubrey’s special ability to nail those long kicks will be neutralized if the Cowboys can’t shore up protection on these field-goal attempts.

Tom – It is more tolerable than satisfying. Those blocks and near blocks are potential game changers and must be avoided. Return yards are a plus, but we still haven’t seen the big return for a score or to get on the doorstep of the end zone.

Sean – The Texans hurt themselves more than the Cowboys with special teams penalties in this game, but the Cowboys left an opportunity to push this differential even further with some sloppiness in the third phase themselves. For a coach that’s been here for a minute now, that’s a tough thing to swallow, and they’ll need to get it corrected. 

Is this the game where the defensvie line have to turn pressures into sacks?

Mike – Yes, absolutely. Tampa Bay has allowed 16 sacks in four games, so if there is ever a week for the Cowboys’ defensive front to arrive, it is this one. Pressures are nice, but against a struggling protection unit, Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Rashaan Gary and the rest of the edge rushers have to finish plays this week. If the Buccaneers offensive line gives them chances and the Cowboys still cannot turn those chances into sacks, then the concern level goes way up. 

Dyllan – The game against Houston was the one where I thought they’d rack up the sacks. And they did finish with two. But I thought it’d come together sooner and more frequently. I’m losing confidence that the current room will be able to get after passers this season.

Jorge – I agree with Dyllan; I’m not sure this group has what it takes to consistently bring the opposing quarterback down. They looked much better at the end of the game and on third down, but we still aren’t seeing much in the rush. I think that Christian Parker has to start maximizing their ability to rush the passer beyond asking them to beat their blockers with their skill/athleticism, so I’m talking more vigorous rush plans, and maybe even more blitzes. 

Tom – The lack of sacks is only concerning when paired with the failure to get a single interception. One can offset the other, but when neither is happening, it just increases the concern about whether this team can ever put it all together on D.

Sean – To Tom’s point, rookie starter Jalon Daniels was sacked three times by the Packers on Sunday, but also threw two interceptions, so the impact plays could go either way, and both would be welcome from Parker’s defense. I would lean towards forcing this quarterback to throw into coverage as much as possible, so the chance for edge rushers to win matchups straight up will be there. I think they’ll get some, but not enough for us to feel drastically better about the EDGE group coming out of the game.

RAPID FIRE 

Who scores first for Dallas?

Dyllan – George Pickens gets on the board first the week.

Jorge – CeeDee Lamb

Tom – Javonte Williams, rapidly becoming a red zone machine

Sean – I think it’s time for me to start picking Pickens until it hits, so Pickens.

CeeDee Lamb receptions, over/under 9.5

Dyllan – Under. This is the week Pickens faces more solo coverage and comes alive.

Jorge – Yeah, under. 

Tom – Ditto

Sean – Ride the hot hand, over for me.

Javonte Williams rushing yards, over/under 79.5

Dyllan – Over. I think Dallas gets up early and it becomes kill the clock time.

Jorge – Over, for the reasons Dyllan mentioned.

Tom – I’ll stick with the under until this team proves it can run the ball effectively outside the red zone

Sean – Under.

Dallas sacks on Jalon Daniels, over/under 3.5

Dyllan – Under. The pass rush is still very suspect regardless of opponent.

Jorge – Under

Tom – Ditto again

Sean – Under

Cowboys margin of victory, over/under 9.5

Dyllan – Over. 10 points is a huge line in the NFL but I think Dallas piles on the points and the defense nets them extra possessions.

Jorge – Under, I’m still not convinced with this coaching staff.

Tom – Over, just because they are about due for a blowout of an outmanned opponent

Sean – Over would sure be nice

True or false? Dallas forces multiple turnovers this week on defense.

Dyllan – True. And I see your multiple turnovers and raise you one defensive touchdown.

Jorge – False

Tom – False until proven otherwise

Sean – Probably false.

item.title: Eagles News: Reflecting on Lane Johnson’s legendary career
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 10/7/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Lane is a legend. While I do think he’s properly getting his flowers following his retirement announcement, I do wish the damper of “How do the Eagles replace him?” wasn’t also a necessary discussion right now. Wish he could’ve made the decision back in the offseason to allow more space for celebrating him without interruption. To be clear, this isn’t to criticize Lane. He clearly wasn’t ready to make the call back then. That’s understandable. Things change. You can’t always anticipate how you’re going to feel down the road. In any case, here’s to one of the greatest Eagles players we’ll ever see. Glad we all got to witness his excellent career and come to know him as a fellow human. I know offensive linemen aren’t the most popular jersey choices for fans but I do hope to see more No. 65s out in the wild.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Eagles legend Lane Johnson retires: Five thoughts on the announcement – PHLY Eagles

1) Lane Johnson is the best player I’ve covered in my eight years reporting on this team. He was the type of ruthlessly efficient offensive tackle that didn’t always grab your attention on a down-in, down-out fashion, but the consistency with which he singlehandedly erased even the league’s top edge rushers solidified his status as one of the best offensive linemen in modern NFL history. Johnson went whole seasons without allowing not only sacks, but pressures during his career. And he did so in a way the Eagles built an entire offensive philosophy around. They’d have two of the league’s best offensive tackles, and they’d leave them both isolated on islands in pass protection as a result. Perhaps that arrangement didn’t get the recognition it deserved throughout Johnson’s career; his five All-Pro honors somehow feel insufficient for the player he was and the impact he had on the game. So did his omission from the NFL’s Top 100 players going into this season (something that didn’t seem lost on him upon his return to training camp a few months ago). None of this should change what most in Philadelphia already know: Johnson was one of the best players of a generation and belongs in the Hall of Fame.

Lane Johnson gave the Eagles greatness. To Philadelphia, he meant something more – The Athletic

“The best …” I can’t tell you how many times during the past decade I’ve heard that word used to describe Lane Johnson — from teammates, coaches, executives. “No question about it in my mind that he’s the best player I’ve ever been around,” Nick Sirianni said. “He’s the best offensive lineman that’s f—ing come through the Eagles,” Cam Jurgens said. “One of the best players ever to play his position in NFL history,” Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie said. “Best tackle in the NFL,” team security chief Dom DiSandro said. “For the past decade, Lane has been the best right tackle in the NFL,” Jason Kelce wrote Tuesday. Saquon Barkley called him the best player on the team. Howie Roseman called him one of the greatest to play the game and said he changed how the NFL views right tackles. Take their word for it.

Taking stock of the Eagles’ offensive line after Lane Johnson’s retirement – BGN

The Eagles’ offensive line situation right now is far from ideal. As a unit, they already weren’t playing very well while healthy. And now they’re losing their best player with Johnson retiring. And it’s not like Jeff Stoutland is here to help get the most out of the remaining talent. The Eagles have had seasons from hell in the past when their offensive line has gone to crap. Unfortunately, 2026 might just be another one of those years.

NFC East Mixtape Vol. 196: Week 5 Preview | Cowboys on TNF | Eagles in London – NFC East Mixtape

A new week is upon us and it is a quick one at that. The Dallas Cowboys will be in action shortly as they will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night. Can they get above .500 for the first time this season? Elsewhere in the division, the Philadelphia Eagles are on the verge of falling apart and a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London just might be the tipping point. Finally, the New York Giants will visit the Washington Commanders and if the home team loses… is their season over? RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss on the latest episode of the NFC East Mixtape! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed!

Jaguars keep climbing in NFL power rankings entering Week 5 – Big Cat Country

The respect is finally coming. After taking care of business in Week 4, the Jacksonville Jaguars now sit at 3-1. They have a convincing first-place lead in the division — and their chances to earn the top seed in the conference continue to rise. “I don’t think we really care about the credit,” safety Antonio Johnson said Monday. “We’re going to go into each week, and if you don’t look at us as an imposing defense, then we’re going to impose our will on you. If you don’t respect us, then we’re going to make you respect us. I know personally, in the rooms that I’ve talked to the players, we don’t care about the respect. You don’t respect us, cool. We’re going to make you respect us, so we’re not even tripping about that.” As Week 5 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense of how the Jaguars are viewed nationally.

Eagles player review: Markel Bell’s debut against the Rams – PhillyVoice

I don’t think Bell is ready to start. Opposing defenses are going to throw everything they can at him, and my guess if that we’re going to see him struggle. I also think the Eagles should just start him anyway. Let him get as many reps as he can, allow him to improve, see what he has, and let his performance guide whether or not the team still needs a replacement for Johnson next offseason, or if Bell shows enough that he can be the guy. However, I do think there’s a chance that the coaching staff might prefer to play the far more experienced Fred Johnson if they still have delusions that they are Super Bowl contenders. Of course, Johnson missed the last two games with a knee injury, so that might not even be an option, for now.

NFL Week 5 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we’re hearing – ESPN

Are any coaches’ seats warming a little early? […] Graziano: Yeah, barring a massive turnaround, you have to think someone ends up in trouble with the Chargers. Head coach? GM? Quarterback? All of the above? Also, what happens if things turn really bad in Philadelphia? Obviously, the Eagles aren’t afraid to move off an offensive coordinator after one disappointing season, but could things get bad enough that Super Bowl-winning head coach Nick Sirianni has to start watching his back? […] Fowler: With Philly, it has been proved that if owner Jeffrey Lurie and GM Howie Roseman identify a problem on the field, they will find a solution. Sometimes that involves the head coach. Another up-and-down season would inevitably keep Sirianni’s name in the leaguewide conversation, despite him winning 70% of his games and having a Super Bowl ring. But this is Philly, where anything is possible.

Why Lane Johnson called it a career four games into the 2026 season, and what’s next for the Eagles – Inquirer

Lane Johnson had thought about retiring along with Jeff Stoutland. The plan was that they’d “go out together,” something they had “talked about before last season,” a source familiar with Johnson’s thinking told The Inquirer. The Hall of Fame-bound right tackle was initially devastated when Stoutland walked away from the Eagles in February, a move that was precipitated by the organization’s decision to change its offense and strip the longtime offensive line coach of his run game coordinator role. “I think it’s my sign,” Johnson told a few confidants at the time. But he didn’t want to make a rash decision. He wanted to hear out Eagles coach Nick Sirianni, new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and Stoutland’s replacement, Chris Kuper. He was encouraged by what he heard about the Kyle Shanahan-Sean McVay scheme they had planned to implement in Philadelphia.

Jordan Mailata reacts to Lane Johnson’s abrupt retirement – NBCSP

Just a couple hours after Lane Johnson abruptly announced his retirement from the NFL on Tuesday afternoon, his teammate Jordan Mailata made an appearance on 94WIP. And Mailata was still processing the news. “Still kind of shocked by it all,” Mailata said to the afternoon show. “Still a hard one to swallow to be honest. To be honest, I’m not going to comment on Lane’s retirement. I don’t want to speak for him or speak on this. I think it’s just heavy. It’s heavy to deal with right now. I’m still processing my emotions, let alone also trying to remember all the times we had. A lot of memories to unpack when I think about Lane. I just think about how much I’m going to miss him moving forward.”

    Eagles DC Vic Fangio: Number of snaps impacted defense against Rams, but have to finish – PFT

    The first Rams scoring drive started at their own 2-yard-line and the second covered 79 yards. Los Angeles only faced two third downs on the 21 snaps that made up those possessions, which led to a question for Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio about whether the cumulative effect of being on the field for 82 snaps — including penalties, but excluding one kneeldown at the end of the game — wore the unit down. “Well, I’m not going to insult your or anybody’s intelligence that yeah, it has an effect, but we got to find a way to finish,” Fangio said, via a transcript from the team.

    Spadaro: Darius Cooper is doing it the right way, on and off the field – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

    Darius Cooper understands the NFL business, so when the Eagles revamped their wide receiver room in the offseason with the additions of Makai Lemon via the NFL Draft and Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore in free agency, there were no guarantees for Cooper. Not that there ever have been, anyway. “I’ve had to work from the bottom my entire career,” he said. “Nothing new here.” That’s the mindset Cooper has had since his college days at Tarleton State from 2020-2024 and it is absolutely the way he has approached the NFL from the moment the Eagles signed him as an undrafted free agent following the 2025 NFL Draft. Cooper earned a spot on the team’s 53-man roster as a rookie, contributed 9 catches, 92 yards, and the role of the “dirty work” wide receiver playing more than 200 snaps on offense, and helping mightily as a special teams player. In his second season, Cooper has taken his game up a notch and we’re all seeing it in living color.

    NFL Power Rankings, Week 5: Cowboys, Pats rising at quarter mark; unbeaten Vikings fall out of top 10 – NFL.com

    21) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. Sunday’s loss to the Rams represented a new low for Philadelphia’s offense, which was missing a collection of key contributors. Its performance could be excused by the absences, including an early exit from Saquon Barkley, but the fashion in which the Eagles let the game slip away is more concerning. Philly’s defense hasn’t been as good as expected, either. This team must figure things out quickly with Jacksonville, Carolina and Dallas up next.

    The Ringer’s Quarter-Season NFL Power Rankings – The Ringer

    17) We could chalk up their early-season struggles to the losses of former offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland and receiver A.J. Brown (now in New England), but these problems existed while both were there—dating back to the team’s Super Bowl–winning season in 2024. What’s changed is that the Eagles defense is no longer the best in football. Now, when the offense stalls, it’s costing this team games, as it did during Los Angeles’s comeback win at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles are trying to prevent things from going totally sideways, but the next stretch of their schedule will require Hurts and this group to keep pace with some great opposing offenses. If Hurts turns in more passing performances like we’ve seen lately, the losing will continue in Philadelphia.

    Steelers sign former Browns defensive end – Behind The Steel Curtain

    Henry had stints with the Eagles in 2024 (on the team for Super Bowl LIX) and 2025.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers are signing defensive end K.J. Henry to their practice squad, Mike Garafolo reports. Henry spent last year with the Cleveland Browns and was most recently with the San Francisco 49ers this past summer.

    Colts sign WR Quez Watkins to practice squad; release CB Elijah Culp from practice squad – Colts.com

    Quez Watkins, 6-0, 193 pounds, has played in 49 career games (25 starts) in his time with the Philadelphia Eagles (2020-23, 2025), Arizona Cardinals (2025) and Pittsburgh Steelers (2024). He has totaled 98 receptions for 1,249 yards (12.7 avg.) and six touchdowns. Watkins has also registered 14 kickoff returns for 200 yards (14.3 avg.). He has appeared in five postseason contests (one start) and has caught six passes for 55 yards (9.2 avg.). Watkins was originally selected by the Eagles in the sixth round (200th overall) of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Southern Miss. In 2025, he spent most of the season on Philadelphia’s practice squad but did not see game action.

    Patriots waive linebacker Jose Ramirez from 53-man roster, make changes to practice squad – Pats Pulpit

    Ramirez, 27, had joined the practice squad in Foxborough as the calendar turned to September after clearing waivers at the NFL’s cutdown deadline. Three weeks later, the 6-foot-2, 252-pound edge rusher was promoted to the active roster. He notched one tackle and appeared in two games from there, seeing 30 snaps between special teams and defense. Entering the NFL in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at No. 196 overall, the former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan checked into four career games before heading to the AFC East. Beginning his run with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Ramirez spent last year with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats before circling back with the Philadelphia Eagles on a futures contract in January

    Buffalo Bills sign defensive back to practice squad with ties to Jim Leonhard – Buffalo Rumblings

    A.J. Woods is high-caliber athlete despite his undrafted status. At the Pittsburgh Pro Day in 2024, he measured in at 5’10” and 187 pounds and ran 4.40 with a 37.5” vertical, 123” broad jump, and a blistering 6.70 time in the three-cone drill. He was a teammate of Bills safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson in 2024 when the Eagles won the Super Bowl.

    Browns bringing in a former CLE WR for a workout before Week 5 vs Jets, reportedly – Dawgs By Nature

    Proche participated in Eagles mandatory minicamp earlier this year on a tryout basis.

    James Proche III could help fill that role if his workout goes well on Tuesday. A sixth-round pick of the Baltimore Ravens in 2020, Proche has played for three teams, including last year with the Tennessee Titans. Primarily a kick return specialist, Proche has only caught 34 passes for 364 yards in 71 career games. He has returned 68 punts and 60 kicks, including 41 punt returns for Cleveland spread over two seasons.

    Khalil Mack trade rumors: Landing spots for the Chargers pass rusher – SB Nation

    Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys are always looking to upgrade their defense and Jerry Jones would likely jump at the chance to add Mack to the mix. Their pass rush has been lacking since trading Micah Parsons last year.

    After a month of games, are the Cowboys a viable playoff team?– Blogging The Boys

    But, the Cowboys have added Joey Porter Jr. The defense seems to be taking incremental steps forward, you can kind of glimpse the future they are shooting for. They will get Tyler Smith back, one of the best players in the league. And given the context of their opponents so far this season, their schedule isn’t as daunting as once thought. But, that is a lot of hoping. The defense very well may stay a liability as the pass rush is anemic. Two sacks against a poor Texans offensive line doesn’t change that. And special teams look like they will let us down at various points this season no matter what.

    6 storylines for NY Giants-Washington Commanders: Prepping for Jayden Daniels – Big Blue View

    The Giants manipulated their roster against the Arizona Cardinals is such a way that McCarthy was QB3, with Harbaugh saying it was “unrealistic” for J.J. McCarthy to be able to function in a full backup role. Harbaugh, though, admitted that there were “certain plays that we had prepared for” McCarthy. They ended up choosing not to use them. That could change this Sunday. Harbaugh said on Monday that McCarthy being the No. 2 quarterback behind Jameis Winston this week is “definitely on the table.” McCarthy is not the runner Jaxson Dart is. In 10 games, he has averaged 3.7 rushes per game for 4.9 yards per carry. Dart, an excellent runner, averages 6.1 rushing attempts per games and 5.6 yards per carry. Still, McCarthy is an athletic 23-year-old who offers the Giants the chance to keep the quarterback run game in the playbook. I am going to guess that we see a little bit of it against the Commanders.

    Is there cause for concern with Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt? – Hogs Haven

    The Commanders run game is a quandary. The commitment to it is fine. Offensive coordinator David Blough continues to call for runs at an appropriate rate. The numbers look just sort of okay. You take away the quarterback runs, though, and an eyebrow gets raised. We aren’t talking about a nuclear winter, here. We’re just making folks aware that the bedrock of this offensive system isn’t hitting on all cylinders. The bottom line stats, as we’ve mentioned, can also be skewed by mobile quarterbacks. Here’s what we’re trying to get to in this long introduction: the curious case of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who is averaging less than four yards per carry over four games. That number dropped to less than two over the last two games, with Rachaad White unavailable on Sunday against the Colts.

The Eagles are making a move to bolster their ailing running back group.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that they will sign Dameon Pierce to the active roster from the practice squad.

Pierce signed with the Eagles in March and returned to the practice squad after being released at the end of the summer. He had four carries for 10 yards in one game for the Chiefs and 10 carries for 26 yards in four games for the Texans last year. He also spent the previous three seasons with the Texans and had 415 carries for 1,674 yards and eight touchdowns over his entire run in Houston.

Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby both left last Sunday's loss to the Rams with injuries. Barkley hurt his hamstring and is questionable for the near future while Bigsby suffered a core muscle injury that requires surgery.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rookie Report: Denzel Boston and Carnell Tate headline a class still trying to find its way
item.description: Ray Garvin examines the impact the 2026 NFL Draft class is having a month into the fantasy football season.
item.content:encoded:
Four weeks into the season, opportunity is beginning to separate the rookie hits from the expensive redraft misses. Four games cannot tell us everything about a rookie class, but that timeline can tell us who is earning opportunities. That is what this Rookie Report is about. We are checking in on the class's top names, what they have produced and whether their usage gives us a reason to believe better fantasy days are coming.

Some rookies are already becoming weekly starters. Others are reminding us why Year 1 expectations need to be handled with care. Let's get into it.

Already earning our trust

Carnell Tate, WR, Tennessee Titans

The situation in Tennessee is bad. I do not expect it to improve quickly, either. The Titans rank 31st in scoring and 31st in plays per game, yet Tate has already established himself as the clear focal point of their passing game. He has 22 receptions for 268 yards through four games, with an 84.1% snap share, 26.9% target share and 36% first-read target share.

Then came the explosion we had been waiting for: nine catches for 145 yards on 12 targets against Baltimore. Tate accounted for 38.7% of Tennessee's targets in that game and finally showed the playmaking ability that made him the fourth overall pick in this year's draft. The offense will continue to create frustrating weeks, and the touchdown opportunities may not be there consistently. Still, this type of usage wins. I do not expect Tate to become a fantasy WR1 this season, but because of the volume, solid WR3 production with occasional spike weeks like we just saw is absolutely on the table.

Denzel Boston, WR, Cleveland Browns

Boston has been the best rookie receiver through the first quarter of the season. He has only 13 receptions, but those catches have produced 284 yards and two touchdowns. His 21.8 yards per reception tell part of the story. His 51.1% share of Cleveland's air yards, second among qualifying NFL receivers, tells us how the Browns are using him.

Deshaun Watson is playing better football, and Boston has emerged as Cleveland's top downfield option while playing 92.2% of the offensive snaps. Ten of his 13 receptions have resulted in either a first down or touchdown, so this is not empty production built on manufactured touches. Cleveland is asking him to make high-value plays, and he is delivering. Boston's 19% target share still leaves room for growth, but he already looks like the rookie receiver I trust most in fantasy lineups. 

KC Concepcion, WR, Cleveland Browns

KC Concepcion is good. He is playing 79% of Cleveland's snaps, has a 24.1% target share and has already accumulated 28 targets. Those are strong rookie usage numbers. The problem is that I believe he is the second-best rookie receiver on his own team.

That distinction matters because Cleveland averages only 29 pass attempts per game. Boston is receiving the valuable downfield opportunities while Concepcion has turned 17 receptions into 144 yards without a touchdown. There are still encouraging signs. KC's snap share climbed to 92.2% in Week 4, and he caught five of eight targets for 64 yards. Better days are ahead because the participation and target volume are real. His ceiling is simply being squeezed by Boston's emergence and a Browns offense that does not create enough volume to consistently support both players.

Rookie roller coaster

Jeremiyah Love, RB, Arizona Cardinals

Jeremiyah Love was the consensus rookie RB1 and fantasy managers drafted him like an immediate difference-maker. Four weeks in, the results have been uneven. He has 55 carries for 223 yards with 11 receptions, 36 receiving yards and two total touchdowns, but one 26-touch performance in Week 3 is doing a lot of the work. Love's season-long snap share sits at only 49.5%, and Arizona followed his breakout by reducing him to 15 touches in Week 4, potentially in part due to an ankle injury.

This is where we have to remember how often rookie running back expectations get out of control. Arizona is installing a new offense under Mike LaFleur, which ranks 20th in EPA per play and has been open about managing Love's workload. LaFleur was the one who stressed that this is a "long season" while explaining the backfield rotation. Love has flashed the talent, but the team and role are not ready to deliver the consistent RB1 production fantasy managers paid for.

He remains a weekly starter, just not the instant superstar many drafted. 

Kenyon Sadiq, TE, New York Jets

Sadiq gave fantasy managers the full rookie tight end experience in two weeks. He erupted for seven catches, 105 yards and a touchdown in Week 3, then failed to catch any of his four targets in Week 4. That is a hard fall back to earth.

The underlying role was better than the box score. Sadiq played a season-high 68.8% of the snaps in Week 4 and commanded 26.7% of the targets. For the season, he has 12 receptions for 143 yards with one receiving touchdown and another score on the ground. Those flashes are real, but the Jets rank 24th in scoring and 28th in plays per game. We have to respect how difficult it is for rookie tight ends to produce consistently. Sadiq remains a worthwhile upside hold, but the Week 3 breakout did not turn him into an automatic weekly starter.

Consider moving on

Jadarian Price, RB, Seattle Seahawks

Price was the only other running back selected in the first round, and his rookie season is quickly turning into one of the class's biggest redraft disappointments. He produced 119 yards on 28 carries across three games, but two lost fumbles, while a 27.2% snap share and minimal receiving involvement kept him from taking control of Seattle's backfield.

Now Price is on injured reserve with a chest injury and will miss at least four games. Seattle also opened Zach Charbonnet's 21-day practice window, creating another obstacle whenever Price is cleared to return. That is frustrating because Price showed legitimate juice and averaged 4.3 yards per carry. The problem was never the flashes. It was the ball security, limited role and now the availability. In standard redraft leagues without an IR spot, Price is getting awfully close to being a drop candidate.

Week 5 consensus Half-PPR Rankings

  • QBs

  • RBs

  • WRs

  • TEs

  • FLEX

  • D/ST

  • Kickers

Consensus Full-PPR Rankings

  • RBs

  • WRs

  • TEs

  • FLEX

Makai Lemon, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

Pour one out for the Makai Lemon redraft dream. He has played 67.4% of Philadelphia's offensive snaps, but that involvement has produced only 10 receptions for 65 yards. The Eagles rank 26th in scoring, 25th in pass attempts and 26th in EPA per play. This is one of the NFL's least productive offenses, and Lemon's role is not creating valuable fantasy opportunities.

Philadelphia is now dealing with another seismic change after future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement. Even DeVonta Smith's absence has not been enough to unlock Lemon. His Week 4 target share rose to 22.2%, but six targets produced only 27 yards. Normally, we want to bet on a talented rookie gaining routes while a veteran is unavailable. Not here.

The deployment, quarterback play and overall offensive environment are working against him. Through four weeks, Lemon has been a colossal redraft miss and can be dropped in standard leagues. 

Stash candidates

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

Antonio Williams is interesting because his official production does not fully capture what he has shown on the field. He opened the season with four receptions for 64 yards and a touchdown, but has produced only eight catches for 60 yards over the past three games. Some of his most explosive work has also disappeared because of penalties, including an 87-yard touchdown in Week 4 that was wiped away by an illegal shift. That play does not count for fantasy, but it matters when evaluating whether Williams can create big plays at this level. 

He also played a season-high 68.8% of Washington's snaps in Week 4, earned eight targets, commanded a 21.6% target share and accounted for 97 official air yards. Washington ranks 12th in pass attempts per game and Williams is already its starting slot receiver, so the environment is there for his role to grow. Terry McLaurin's absence may have inflated that Week 4 opportunity, but Williams is a worthwhile stash whose fantasy production could look much different if those explosive plays begin counting. He's rostered in 6% of Yahoo leagues.

Fernando Mendoza, QB, Las Vegas Raiders

Mendoza has not played a regular-season snap, so this is a Superflex stash based entirely on environment and contingency value. The Raiders have been much better than advertised. They rank eighth in scoring, fourth in plays per game and 11th in EPA per play. Kirk Cousins has thrown 11 touchdown passes, tied for the league lead, with three three-touchdown games.

Some of that is Cousins, but Klint Kubiak deserves credit. Las Vegas has built a creative offense around Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ashton Jeanty, using 12 personnel and heavier formations to manufacture favorable matchups. The Raiders still lack a traditional No. 1 receiver, yet the system is generating points. Mendoza is officially the QB2 behind Cousins, so there is no immediate path while the veteran is healthy. If an opportunity opens later in the season, Mendoza would be stepping into an offense capable of making him a streamable fantasy quarterback. 

Jordyn Tyson, WR, New Orleans Saints

Tyson remains on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury in August, but he is one of my favorite end-of-bench stashes where an IR spot is available. New Orleans ranks second in offensive plays and first with 45 pass attempts per game. This team is playing fast, throwing constantly and spending plenty of time chasing points.

Look at what DeVaughn Vele has done with that opportunity. He has 21 receptions for 226 yards and two touchdowns through four games. Vele has been more than serviceable, but Tyson was the eighth overall pick because he offers another level of separation and playmaking. Can a healthy Tyson eventually absorb some of those routes and targets? That is the bet. His original recovery timeline was approximately two months, so this may not help fantasy managers immediately. Even if Tyson only contributes during the closing weeks of the fantasy season, this passing environment gives him enough upside to justify the stash.

Final thoughts

Four weeks gives us enough information to evaluate roles, not enough to write the final story. Tate, Boston and Concepcion are earning sustainable opportunities. Love, Williams and Sadiq are showing us the talent without giving us weekly stability. Price and Lemon remind us that draft cost does not guarantee immediate production.
